claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 10,000 infantry and 2,700 cavalry, total 12,700; side B (Spanish) 10,000 infantry and 2,500 cavalry, total 12,500.

claims.value: Jourdan gives side A 11,000–12,000 combatants in the assembled corps before the Ciudad Real advance.
claims.rationale: The paragraph continues the corps assembly from the preceding page; not the isolated cavalry screen or all simultaneously engaged troops. English rendering (ours): "In all, 11,000 to 12,000 combatants."

claims.value: Jourdan gives side B 12,000 infantry and 3,000 cavalry with 14 guns when Cartojal assembled against Milhaud.
claims.rationale: French opponent estimate; the sequence distinguishes Milhaud’s advanced division from Sebastiani’s arriving infantry. English rendering (ours): "Cartojal, seeing the division unsupported, assembled his army: 12,000 infantry, 3,000 cavalry and fourteen guns."

claims.value: Jourdan places Milhaud over the advance cavalry and Sebastiani arriving with the infantry before the bridge attack.
claims.rationale: Specific contingent and corps tasks, not equal credit for listed officers. English rendering (ours): "Milhaud’s division followed closely and crossed the Guadiana; meanwhile Sebastiani arrived with his infantry."

claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "The armies faced one another across the Guadiana, with a bridge that had not been cut."

A.command_scope: Printed label and additional local/superior observations remain separate. Bodart lists side A under Sebastiani; side B under Cartaojal. Jourdan places Milhaud over the advance cavalry and Sebastiani arriving with the infantry before the bridge attack.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity; repeated commanders or formation names are insufficient.
